# idkcraft — project review profile

## What this is
A hobby Minecraft stack: Paper server (`mc`), a Node 22 mineflayer bot (`bot/src`), and a CPU
"System-1" brain sidecar (`laya/shim.py`, FastAPI-shaped REST). Deployed by GitOps to Portainer.
The owner treats it as a learning project: changes should be readable and explain themselves.

## What a real failure looks like
- The bot crash-loops, disconnects, or stops ticking (`BRAIN_TICK_MS` loop stalls, unhandled
  promise rejection, mineflayer event never handled).
- The bot spams the remote brain when no player is online (cost guard in README is deliberate).
- A behaviour steals the tick from another one (follow stops while scouting, fight never yields).
- Secrets, hostnames, domains or IPs land in the repo (privacy rule in CLAUDE.md) — **critical**.
- A change to `docker-compose.yml` service names, env var names or the `laya` REST shape breaks the
  deployed stack (shared contract in CLAUDE.md, "do not rename").

## Blast radius
One private server, a handful of players. Wrong bot behaviour is annoying, not dangerous. A leaked
hostname or key is the one thing that cannot be taken back.

## Reporting bar
Report what breaks at runtime in the bot loop, in tests, or in the deploy contract. `npm test` in
`bot/` runs without a Minecraft client (fake-player harness) — a change that needs a live server to
be verified at all should say so, and a missing assertion for new branching logic is a finding.

## Deliberate conventions
- Ponytail rules: smallest diff, no speculative abstractions, one brain interface. A
  `// ponytail:` comment marks an intentional shortcut with its ceiling — not a finding.
- `ONLINE_MODE=false` + `ENFORCE_WHITELIST=TRUE`: intentional, the bot has no Microsoft account.
- Stub brain must keep working when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` / brain URL is absent.
- Plain CommonJS, no TypeScript, no framework beyond mineflayer + its plugins.

1	# Round 01 findings (both addressed)
2	
3	## loop+goal-1 [minor] Paused branch ticks the scout with nobody online, unlike the idle branch
4	The paused block runs the scout seam unconditionally (lines 64-65), outside the `if (target) / else` above it, whereas the normal path only reaches the scout seam after `if (!target) return ...` (lines 79-95) — scout never scans when nobody is online. `bot/test/tick.test.js:220` pins that invariant for the unpaused path ("never scans or chats when no player is online").
5	
6	Trigger: a player says `stop` (paused = true), then everyone logs off. `findTarget` returns null (confirmed in `bot/src/perception.js:22` — empty `bot.players` yields `null`), so `lastVisible` is false and the loop settles into the 10 s poll, but every one of those ticks still creates the scout (registry is present after spawn) and calls `scout.tick()`.
7	
8	Consequences, in order of weight: (a) `bot.findBlocks` runs every 10 s indefinitely with no audience; (b) the veins it finds are added to the scout's `seen` set and chatted into an empty server, so a player who logs back in while the bot is still parked never hears about the ore around it — scout's `seen` set is per-instance and persists on `ctx.scout`. Note the chat/console burst is one-time, not indefinite: a parked bot is stationary, so after the first scan nothing is `fresh` and the loop goes quiet. The comment at lines 51-53 claiming the paused path is the "same cost guard as 'no player online'" is therefore slightly inaccurate as written.
9	
10	The root cause is that the paused block is a hand-copy of the idle cost-guard block (lines 79-95) with the scout seam spliced in at a different nesting level.
11	FIX: Move lines 64-65 inside the `if (target)` arm of the paused block so the scout only ticks when a player is visible, matching the unpaused path. The move stays inside the paused branch — no signature or caller change.
12	
13	## loop+goal-2 [minor] New paused test never exercises the scout seam, the one thing the bead says pausing must preserve

# idkcraft — Paper+Geyser server (mc) + follow bot (bot) + LAYA brain (laya).
# No Traefik: Minecraft is raw TCP/UDP, host ports are published directly.
# Service names (mc, bot, laya) and bot env names are the shared contract
# with the bot bead (bot/**) — do not rename.
#
# Geyser Floodgate auth is declarative (bring-up 2026-09-21 proved Geyser
# 2.11 does NOT switch to Floodgate auth just because Floodgate is
# installed — a generated config stays auth-type: online, which blocks
# Bedrock joins). an inline configs entry (via PATCH_DEFINITIONS)
# sets java.auth-type=floodgate in /data/plugins/Geyser-Spigot/config.yml.
# Timing: the file only exists after Geyser's first run, so on a truly fresh
# volume the first boot logs a patch skip warning and comes up online; the
# next start (restart/redeploy) applies floodgate, and every start after
# that keeps it. Do not vendor a full Geyser config.yml
# (drifts every Geyser release).

services:
  mc:
    # Date tag pinned 2026-09-21; this tag ships Java 25 (Paper 26.x needs >= 25).
    image: itzg/minecraft-server:${MC_IMAGE_TAG:-2026.9.1}
    container_name: ${MC_CONTAINER_NAME:-idkcraft-mc}
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    ports:
      - "${MC_JAVA_PORT:-25565}:25565"
      - "${MC_BEDROCK_PORT:-19132}:19132/udp"
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: PAPER
      # Pin rationale lives in .env.example (newest Paper both Geyser and
      # mineflayer support as of 2026-09-21).
      VERSION: ${MC_VERSION:-26.1.2}
      INIT_MEMORY: ${MC_INIT_MEMORY:-512M}
      MAX_MEMORY: ${MC_MAX_MEMORY:-2G}
      ONLINE_MODE: "false"
      ENFORCE_WHITELIST: "TRUE"
      # Offline UUID of IdkBot (server runs ONLINE_MODE=false, so Paper matches
      # the whitelist by UUID; a name would resolve to an online UUID and the
      # bot would be rejected). If BOT_USERNAME changes, recompute:
      # python3 -c 'import uuid,hashlib;print(uuid.UUID(bytes=hashlib.md5(b"OfflinePlayer:IdkBot").digest(),version=3))'
      WHITELIST: ${WHITELIST:-3d1f4b94-9298-3ba3-af2d-3f73ce56138f}
      OPS: ${OPS:-}
      DIFFICULTY: ${MC_DIFFICULTY:-easy}
      MOTD: idkcraft
      PATCH_DEFINITIONS: /patches
      # Geyser/Floodgate/ViaVersion track "latest" — drift risk accepted for
      # iteration 1. ViaVersion is needed because Geyser emulates a 26.2 Java
      # client, so a Paper server below 26.2 must accept newer clients
      # (https://geysermc.org/wiki/geyser/supported-versions/); drop it once
      # the server pin reaches a version mineflayer speaks natively.

        https://download.geysermc.org/v2/projects/geyser/versions/latest/builds/latest/downloads/spigot
        https://download.geysermc.org/v2/projects/floodgate/versions/latest/builds/latest/downloads/spigot
        https://api.spiget.org/v2/resources/19254/download

    # image's bundled mc-health script; start_period covers first boot

      MC_HOST: mc
      MC_PORT: 25565
      BOT_USERNAME: ${BOT_USERNAME:-IdkBot}
      BOT_FOLLOW: ${BOT_FOLLOW:-}
      BRAIN_TICK_MS: ${BRAIN_TICK_MS:-1000}
      BRAIN_URL: ${BRAIN_URL:-http://laya:8000/v1/systemone}
      BRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS: ${BRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS:-3000}
      TYPESAFE_API_KEY: ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY:-}

  laya:
    # Built by CI from ./laya and pushed to GHCR.
    # :latest is a placeholder — CI rewrites it to the commit sha on deploy.
    image: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya:latest
    container_name: ${LAYA_CONTAINER_NAME:-idkcraft-laya}
    restart: unless-stopped
    # 2g contract replaced by 3g (2026-09-21: prod OOM-killed the sidecar
    # under 2g at load; host budget still fits: mc 6g + laya 3g + ~5.2g other).
    mem_limit: ${LAYA_MEM_LIMIT:-3g}

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "python -c \"import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', timeout=3)\""]

name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate compose config
        run: |
          docker compose --env-file .env.example config -q

      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Tag each image by its directory TREE hash, so pushes that change
      # neither bot/ nor laya/ rebuild nothing (host disk filled up from one
      # image per push; Portainer never prunes old tags). Content-addressed:
      # a revert or rebase reuses the existing image. A docs-only push still
      # redeploys with the same tags — intended, no new image lands.
      - name: Resolve image tags
        run: |
          BOT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD:bot)
          LAYA_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD:laya)
          [ -n "$BOT_SHA" ] && [ -n "$LAYA_SHA" ] || exit 1
          echo "BOT_SHA=${BOT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "LAYA_SHA=${LAYA_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Check bot image
        id: check-bot
        env:
          IMAGE_BASE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft
          BOT_SHA: ${{ env.BOT_SHA }}
        run: |
          if docker manifest inspect "${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        if: steps.check-bot.outputs.build == 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./bot
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft:${{ env.BOT_SHA }}

      - name: Check laya image
        id: check-laya
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          if docker manifest inspect "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./laya
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya:${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=laya
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=laya

      - name: Smoke test laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          docker run -d --name laya-smoke --memory=3g -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 -p 8000:8000 "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}"
          trap "docker logs laya-smoke; docker rm -f laya-smoke" EXIT
          python3 laya/smoke.py http://127.0.0.1:8000

      - name: Push laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          docker push "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}"

      - name: Update deploy branch
        env:
          IMAGE_BASE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          BOT_SHA: ${{ env.BOT_SHA }}
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
          GITHUB_COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B deploy
          sed -i "s|image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:.*|image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}|" docker-compose.yml
          sed -i "s|image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:.*|image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}|" docker-compose.yml
          if ! grep -q "image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}" docker-compose.yml || ! grep -q "image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}" docker-compose.yml; then
            echo "compose image line not rewritten"
            exit 1
          fi
          git add docker-compose.yml
          git commit -m "deploy: ${GITHUB_COMMIT_SHA}"
          git push origin deploy --force

      - name: Trigger Portainer webhook
        uses: distributhor/workflow-webhook@2381f0e9c7b6bf061fb1405bd0804b8706116369 # v3.0.8
        with:
          webhook_url: ${{ secrets.PORTAINER_REDEPLOY_HOOK }}

          IMAGE_BASE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft
          BOT_SHA: ${{ env.BOT_SHA }}
        run: |
          if docker manifest inspect "${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        if: steps.check-bot.outputs.build == 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./bot
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft:${{ env.BOT_SHA }}

      - name: Check laya image
        id: check-laya
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          if docker manifest inspect "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Build laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ./laya
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya:${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=laya
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=laya

      - name: Smoke test laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          docker run -d --name laya-smoke --memory=3g -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 -p 8000:8000 "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}"
          trap "docker logs laya-smoke; docker rm -f laya-smoke" EXIT
          python3 laya/smoke.py http://127.0.0.1:8000

      - name: Push laya image
        if: steps.check-laya.outputs.build == 'true'
        env:
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
        run: |
          docker push "${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}"

      - name: Update deploy branch
        env:
          IMAGE_BASE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft
          LAYA_IMAGE: ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft-laya
          BOT_SHA: ${{ env.BOT_SHA }}
          LAYA_SHA: ${{ env.LAYA_SHA }}
          GITHUB_COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B deploy
          sed -i "s|image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:.*|image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}|" docker-compose.yml
          sed -i "s|image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:.*|image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}|" docker-compose.yml
          if ! grep -q "image: ${IMAGE_BASE}:${BOT_SHA}" docker-compose.yml || ! grep -q "image: ${LAYA_IMAGE}:${LAYA_SHA}" docker-compose.yml; then
            echo "compose image line not rewritten"
            exit 1
          fi
          git add docker-compose.yml
          git commit -m "deploy: ${GITHUB_COMMIT_SHA}"
          git push origin deploy --force

      - name: Trigger Portainer webhook
        uses: distributhor/workflow-webhook@2381f0e9c7b6bf061fb1405bd0804b8706116369 # v3.0.8
        with:
          webhook_url: ${{ secrets.PORTAINER_REDEPLOY_HOOK }}
